# CPG Growth Studio

> CPG Growth Studio is a fractional CMO and retail launch partner for pet food, pet health and CPG brands in the US and Canada. It is led by Ahmed, a former Nestlé Purina, Hill's Pet Nutrition, Moose Toys and Reckitt marketing leader, who gets brands into retailers like PetSmart, Petco, Walmart and Amazon and builds the plan that keeps them selling.

## Who it's for
Founders of pet food, pet treats, pet supplement and vet, snack, protein and functional nutrition, and toy brands, usually $2M to $25M in sales, selling or about to sell into big retailers or Amazon.

## About Ahmed
- 10+ years running brands at Nestlé Purina (Pro Plan Veterinary Diets and Supplements, including FortiFlora), Hill's Pet Nutrition (Colgate-Palmolive), Moose Toys and Reckitt (Lanacane).
- Managed $100M+ and $18M brand portfolios. Won endcaps and launches with Walmart and PetSmart buyers. Built Amazon programs from scratch.
- Retailers sold into: Walmart, PetSmart, Amazon, Pet Valu, Canadian Tire and Indigo.
- Launched FortiFlora PRO, Calming Care, Joint Care and Multi Care at Purina.
- Founder of SondarLogic, an AI company for receipt validation and shopper data.

## Results
- **FortiFlora** (Nestlé Purina): 100%+ brand growth and #1 share in both vet and retail, with no loss of vet clinic sales. [https://www.cpggrowthstudio.com/work/fortiflora/]
- **EssentialCare** (Nestlé Purina): +10.1 share points, moving from a distant #3 to a strong #2 in the category. [https://www.cpggrowthstudio.com/work/essentialcare/]
- **Gui Gui** (Moose Toys): 96% sell-through in 5 weeks, the #2 toy item in Canada, and 5x return on earned media. [https://www.cpggrowthstudio.com/work/gui-gui/]
- **Hill's Science Diet** (Colgate-Palmolive): 200% growth and Subscribe & Save up from 28% to 40%, with a best-in-class Amazon playbook for the brand. [https://www.cpggrowthstudio.com/work/hills-amazon/]

## Services and pricing
- **Growth Audit**: $6,500 one-time · 3 weeks. Review of your retailers, Amazon and pricing; Where you're losing margin; A 90-day action plan; Fee credited if we keep working.
- **Retail Launch**: $3,500 per month · 6-month minimum. Buyer intros through the retail brokers on my team; Buyer-ready pitch and line review plan; Pricing, promo and sell-through plan; Plus 7% of net sales at the retailers we open, for 24 months.
- **Fractional CMO**: $9,500 per month · 6-month minimum. About 1.5 days a week; Owns your marketing plan and budget; Buyer pitches and retail plans; Manages agencies and Amazon.
- **AI Growth Engine**: From $15K setup + $1,500 / month. A rewards program shoppers join by scanning any store receipt; Know who buys you at PetSmart, Walmart and Amazon; Emails and texts that bring them back: welcome, reorder reminders, win-back; Rebates that drive trial without cutting your shelf price.
- Retail Launch includes retail brokers on the CPG Growth Studio team for buyer introductions. The broker's commission is included in the 7% sales share. The share applies only to retailers and items opened together, for 24 months from each one's first order.
- After the first 6 months: ongoing support from $1,500 a month, or Fractional CMO.

## Guides
- [How to get your pet brand into PetSmart, Petco and Walmart](https://www.cpggrowthstudio.com/insights/get-pet-brand-into-petsmart-petco-walmart/): Retail buyers say yes when you prove four things: your product will sell, the margin works for them, you'll send shoppers to the shelf, and you can supply it on time. Build that proof before you pitch, get the meeting at the right point in the buyer's review calendar, and plan your first 90 days of sell-through before the first order ships.
- [What does a fractional CMO cost for a CPG brand?](https://www.cpggrowthstudio.com/insights/fractional-cmo-cost/): Most fractional CMOs in North America charge roughly $5,000 to $15,000 a month, depending on hours and scope. Mine is $9,500 a month for about 1.5 days a week. A full-time CMO often costs $250,000 or more a year once you add salary, bonus and benefits, so a fractional CMO gives a growing brand senior leadership for a fraction of that.
- [How to grow Amazon Subscribe & Save for a pet brand](https://www.cpggrowthstudio.com/insights/amazon-subscribe-and-save-pet-brands/): Fix your digital shelf first, then buy traffic, then reward subscribing instead of one-off deals. At Hill's Science Diet in Canada, that order grew Amazon sales 200% and lifted Subscribe & Save from 28% to 40%.
- [Fractional CMO for pet brands: what one does and when you need one](https://www.cpggrowthstudio.com/insights/fractional-cmo-pet-brands/): A fractional CMO for a pet brand is a senior marketer who works with you part-time to own the plan that grows sales: which retailers to win, how to price, how to launch, and how to turn first-time buyers into repeat ones. You need one when you're about to pitch big retailers, a launch has stalled, or the founder is still running marketing alongside everything else.
- [How to launch your CPG brand in Canadian retail](https://www.cpggrowthstudio.com/insights/launch-cpg-brand-canadian-retail/): Canada has fewer retailers than the US, so each buyer matters more and a bad first launch is hard to recover from. Plan for bilingual packaging, prices that work in Canadian dollars after freight and duty, and a sell-through plan for a smaller market. Then go to the buyers with sales proof, ideally through a broker who already calls on them.
- [Pet supplement marketing: how to grow beyond the vet clinic](https://www.cpggrowthstudio.com/insights/pet-supplement-marketing/): Pet supplements grow when vets recommend them and pet owners can easily rebuy them. Give each channel a clear job, with vets for trust and retail and online for reach and repeat. Turn clinical claims into plain benefits that stay compliant, and make reordering automatic. That's how FortiFlora more than doubled and became #1 in both vet and retail.
- [How to grow a pet brand on Chewy](https://www.cpggrowthstudio.com/insights/grow-pet-brand-on-chewy/): Chewy rewards pet brands that people reorder. Get the product page right, make Autoship the easy choice, build reviews early, and keep promotions focused on repeat rather than one-off deals. Treat Chewy as its own channel with its own plan, not a copy of Amazon.
